groups.title: PostgreSQL-Specific Features
groups.question: Explain some PostgreSQL features that go beyond plain tables and when you would use them.

followUps.JSONB — Semi-Structured Data in Postgres: Why would you choose jsonb over json, and when should a field be a normal column instead?
followUps.Views & Materialized Views: When would you use a materialized view instead of a regular view, and what is the main risk?

evidence.text: jsonb is stored parsed in binary form, so it can be indexed (GIN) and queried without reparsing.
json is stored as text and reparsed on every access.
Fields you filter, join or constrain often should be normal columns.

notEnough: Only naming the terms (json, jsonb, GIN) without explaining how they work or why they matter.

misconceptions.text: Says jsonb should replace normal columns everywhere.

evidence.text: A normal view re-runs its query every time it's read.
A materialized view stores the result, so reads are fast for expensive queries.
It must be refreshed, otherwise it silently serves stale data.

notEnough: Only naming the terms (view, materialized view) without explaining how they work or why they matter.

misconceptions.text: Says a normal view caches its result.

groups.title: PL/pgSQL & Server-Side Logic
groups.question: Walk through the pros and cons of putting logic inside the database server.

followUps.Stored Procedures & Functions in PL/pgSQ: What makes a stored function risky to maintain, and how should it handle errors?
followUps.Triggers — Power & Pitfalls: Why can heavy use of triggers make a system hard to debug?

evidence.text: Logic in the database saves round trips for multi-step work.
Functions are harder to version, test and debug than app code, and easy to forget.
They should raise errors (or handle specific exceptions and re-raise), never swallow them silently.

notEnough: Only naming the terms (PL/pgSQL, stored procedure) without explaining how they work or why they matter.

misconceptions.text: Says catching and ignoring all errors in a function is safe.

evidence.text: Triggers run automatically on inserts, updates or deletes.
Someone reading the app code can't see that a write also changes other tables.
That hidden coupling makes bugs and performance problems hard to trace.

notEnough: Only naming the terms (trigger) without explaining how they work or why they matter.

misconceptions.text: Says triggers have no performance or debugging cost.

groups.title: Extensions & Full-Text Search
groups.question: Explain how PostgreSQL can handle search and specialized data without adding another system.

followUps.PostgreSQL Extensions — PostGIS, pg_trgm: Why is LIKE '%term%' slow, and how does pg_trgm help?
followUps.Full-Text Search with tsvector & tsquery: Why should you store a ready-made tsvector instead of building it inside every search query?

evidence.text: LIKE '%term%' can't use a normal index because of the leading wildcard, so it scans every row.
pg_trgm splits text into three-letter pieces and indexes them (GIN/GiST).
That makes substring and fuzzy searches use an index.

notEnough: Only naming the terms (LIKE, pg_trgm) without explaining how they work or why they matter.

misconceptions.text: Says a normal B-tree index speeds up LIKE '%term%'.

evidence.text: A tsvector is the text broken into normalised words, and a tsquery is the search.
Building the tsvector inside every query reprocesses every row's text on every search.
Storing it (generated column or trigger) lets you index it with GIN and search fast.

notEnough: Only naming the terms (tsvector, tsquery) without explaining how they work or why they matter.

misconceptions.text: Says full-text search is the same as LIKE.

groups.title: psql & Administration
groups.question: Walk through how you would look after a PostgreSQL database day to day.

followUps.psql Meta-Commands & Productivity: Which psql meta-commands do you rely on, and why are they faster than writing catalog queries?
followUps.VACUUM, ANALYZE & Autovacuum: Why do dead rows build up in PostgreSQL, and what happens to query plans if ANALYZE doesn't run?

evidence.text: Backslash commands are psql shortcuts, not SQL.
Names useful ones like \d to describe a table, \dt to list tables, \x for expanded output, \copy for import/export.
One short command replaces writing catalog queries by hand.

notEnough: Only naming the terms (psql, \d) without explaining how they work or why they matter.

misconceptions.text: Says meta-commands are SQL that runs on the server.

evidence.text: Updates and deletes leave old row versions (dead tuples) because of MVCC.
VACUUM (and autovacuum) cleans them up; without it tables bloat and scans slow down.
ANALYZE refreshes statistics; stale stats make the planner choose bad plans.

notEnough: Only naming the terms (VACUUM, ANALYZE, autovacuum) without explaining how they work or why they matter.

misconceptions.text: Says DELETE frees the space immediately.
